answer: Every agent must berth in one harbor, and berths are priced by occupancy: the k-th berth of an epoch costs k times the base fee, so n identities cost n(n+1)/2 base fees, a strictly superlinear marginal cost. A berth binds to a hardware attestation key that cannot be exported; moving an identity to a fresh key forfeits berth history and any marble reputation earned, and an ocean-wide replay rejects two active berths sharing one attestation. Resetting stays legal but pointless: a reborn identity pays the current priciest berth fee while its old tenure is erased.
